title: Let the site's own Content-Security-Policy allow Google's analytics and Ads conversion calls, which it blocks today

source.ref: Production audit 2026-11-10 (owner's Mac, read-only): every audited page logs 5 CSP connect-src violations for analytics.google.com, stats.g.doubleclick.net and www.google.com/g/collect. Google Ads campaign 'Find your people locally' is live with a $500 budget.

detail:
connect-src in next.config.ts allows www.google-analytics.com and region1.google-analytics.com only. The browser blocks Google's calls to analytics.google.com, stats.g.doubleclick.net and www.google.com/g/collect, so conversion and remarketing measurement can silently drop while ads spend. Verify the blocked hosts from a real signed-out page console first (the audit read the first row only), then add exactly those hosts to connect-src (and any matching img-src), nothing wildcard. Never send persona or wellness data to pixels. Coordinate with the Google Ads conversion tracking thread. Done when: a production console on / shows no connect-src violations for those hosts and the conversion fires in Google Ads.

Added analytics.google.com, stats.g.doubleclick.net, www.google.com/g/collect to connect-src; contract test holds them
